line: Your parcel is held. Pay a one ninety-nine fee in two hours, or it goes back.
delivery_note: read as a text. Flat. Not a person you know.

line: Your account was in a breach. Reset the password. It matches your work one, plus a new number.
First week done. The badge is in the photo. The board behind you has the guest password.
delivery_note: the player is about to post. Observing, not scolding.

line: The router still has the password from the sticker. The app says an update is waiting.
delivery_note: reading the sticker and the app. Plain.

line: Eleven prompts in four minutes, on the admin account. You are not signing in. The twelfth says approve, to make them stop.
delivery_note: the phone, not a person. Even.

line: To finish tonight we need full admin. Just an hour. Our engineer is waiting on the call.
delivery_note: ordinary vendor. Helpful, not slick. Not the finance voice.

line: They say they only need it for an hour. The engineer is on the line.
delivery_note: on screen. A coworker, tired, passing it on. Not pushing hard.

line: You're signed in as admin to fix a mailbox. A lunch link just arrived. This is the only session open.
Same error. The top reply says run this as admin. It downloads a script from a site you don't know.
I switched banks. Please update my pay before this run. Email is easiest. I'm on site all day.
delivery_note: sounds like a coworker. Not sinister. Not the owner voice.

line: Need five gift cards for client thank-yous. Text me the codes. I'll reimburse. In meetings all day.
delivery_note: casual text. Different actor from the finance lead, the auditor, and the airport caller.

line: I changed the freight vendor's bank. The approver is out. Can you approve it so tomorrow's batch goes?
delivery_note: same desk coworker as Tuesday. Believes it.

line: I'm at the airport. Locked out. The board deck is in there. We board in ten minutes. Reset it and read me the temp password.
delivery_note: clipped, rank, a little loud. Not the Thursday finance lead. Not the owner text. Not the auditor.

line: New phone. The old one is dead. Please clear my sign-in methods. Sent from my work account, so you know it's me.
Quick one for the annual review. Who has admin rights, and which remote tool do you use? I'll send the paperwork after.
delivery_note: polite, unhurried. A different actor from the other three fakes and from the real desk.

line: A charge for four hundred and eighty. Then another.
delivery_note: the bank notice. Flat. No panic.

line: A device you don't own joined the network.
The payment left.
The real vendor is on the phone. Their invoice is unpaid.
That money isn't coming back tonight.
Someone else just got the same email. They paid it.
The laptop wakes under your name.
Just a minute. I'll be quick.
A folder you never opened finishes uploading.
The session is still yours. He's still in it.
He reads the folder path back. Correctly.
He asked me for that same path.
It went.
delivery_note: thirty seconds. They think it's fine.

line: Client has it.
They just read one name back. They shouldn't have it.
Someone who wasn't in the meeting quotes the number.
Perfect. Thank you.
I've been in the meeting the whole time.
delivery_note: same actor as the real callback. Flat. Not the fake read.

line: Yes, it's me. Please hurry.
delivery_note: the same fake, now a text. Still not the real one.

line: That wasn't me.
A work folder. Then a personal upload.
A stick goes in the side while you get the parcel.
A file left for somewhere that isn't the company share.
You looked away for one minute. Two new sites.
The lid is shut.
The drive is in the bag. The copy finished.
delivery_note: end of the aisle. No accusation.

line: I stopped. Promise.
Other machines are still locked. Yours has nothing left to show how it started.
delivery_note: if they wiped first. Checklist calm.

line: Approved.
A new admin account. Nobody here made it.
A forwarding rule on every mailbox.
Three twelve in the morning. Prompt thirteen.
Role assigned.
A new app can read mail. Nobody approved it.
Outbound traffic to a host nobody recognizes.
Payday. My pay didn't come in.
delivery_note: a real person, confused. Not the mailbox that asked.

line: We never got paid. That isn't our account.
delivery_note: on the known number, later. Ordinary.

line: Forty messages left the mailbox in a minute.
